posts.name: Himanshu Rastogi
posts.cooked:
please explain this error:

hr@pc:~$ ls -R | vi
Vim: Warning: Input is not from a terminal
Vim: Error reading input, exiting...
Vim: preserving files...
Vim: Finished.








hr@pc:~$ ls | vi
Vim: Warning: Input is not from a terminal
Vim: Error reading input, exiting...
Vim: preserving files...
Vim: Finished.
hr@pc:~$ ls | nano
Standard input is not a terminal
hr@pc:~$

@Afnan_POD
@Puneet_21f3002005
@chaitanya353535

posts.name: Chaitanya Mishra
posts.cooked:
It is in the way vi handles the input. If you’d like to do that try ls -R > anyfile
and then
vi anyfile

posts.name: Chaitanya Mishra
posts.cooked:
Vi takes in an argument(filename) and opens it in interactive mode. But when you pass the output through pipe, it cannot open that in interactive mode. You cannot type, delete etc since the input is as a redirect and not as a file where edits can take place. I hope you got the point. And if you are still willing there’s an option
ls -R | vi -
using this you can make it open it as a file in the buffer.

posts.name: Himanshu Rastogi
posts.cooked: got it sir,
